solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Christian joined daughters in lift (9)

indicatorNotes.in: D goes into the word for lift

annotation.surface: A Christian convert is said to have joined when daughters were raised up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like the elevator a daughter rides; it is the verb hoist, and D is dropped into it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a member of the Protestant church founded by John Wesley.

entries.clue: Island whisky that’s top of the list? (5)

blocks.note: a malt is a malt whisky
A heads the alphabet and is the top grade

annotation.surface: A whisky from an island that ranks first on the drinks list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top of the list' is not a first letter here (that would give T); it is A, the grade that heads any ranking.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain example: this Mediterranean nation off Sicily is a small archipelago whose main landmass gives it its name.

entries.clue: Mark slept naked — something artist might draw with delight (6,4)

indicatorNotes.naked: stripped of its outer layer, so SLEPT loses its first and last letters

annotation.surface: An artist's life-drawing model is marked as having slept in the nude.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash parts wordplay from the definition. 'Draw' tempts toward a pencil, but the answer needs INK.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being tickled pink means being so pleased you blush, so the verb phrase matches delight.

entries.clue: Escort on the road in unacceptable condition (8)

blocks.note: out = not acceptable, as in 'that idea is out'
a rider is a condition attached to an agreement

annotation.surface: A road escort in a bad state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In unacceptable condition' reads as one phrase about a shabby car; split it, and 'condition' is a contract's rider.
annotation.definitionFit: An outrider is a motorcyclist escorting a vehicle on the road.

entries.clue: During day in Rome, lira has no purpose (5)

indicatorNotes.During: L comes during, so inside, the Roman day

blocks.note: the Ides was a day in the Roman calendar

annotation.surface: A tourist in Rome finds the old lira useless for the day.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ides fell mid-month in the Roman calendar (March 15th is the famous one).
annotation.definitionFit: Something that idles runs without doing any work, so has no purpose.

entries.clue: Accept children disagree (4,5)

blocks.note: issue = offspring, a legal word for children

annotation.surface: An order to take in children who argue.
annotation.walkthrough: ISSUE for children is legal language, as in 'died without issue'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to take issue is to object or argue against a view, which is disagreeing.

entries.clue: Bold move, Conservative changing old EU pact (4,6)

annotation.surface: A Tory makes a daring play by rewriting a treaty with Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface fits Brexit so well that the French answer hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A coup d'éclat is a brilliant, striking stroke: a bold move.

entries.clue: Chicken half-hearted chef eats cold (4)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: COOK has a double-O heart; half of it goes
indicatorNotes.eats: to eat is to take something inside, so the chef takes C into its body

blocks.note: COOK with one of its two middle Os gone

annotation.surface: A cook who does not care much has a cold chicken dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The heart of COOK is OO, so losing half of it leaves COK, and C goes in the gap.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the male bird of domestic poultry, also called a rooster in America.

entries.clue: Fearless abseiler’s head splits having not tied the knot (6)

indicatorNotes.head: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.splits: A breaks into the word for unmarried

annotation.surface: A bold abseiler's head injury comes from a fall, as the knot was never tied.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tied the knot' pulls toward ropes, fitting the abseiler; it means marriage.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: not overawed or intimidated, so showing no fear.

entries.clue: Drunk’s face certainly cheerful — bar adding an hour to time? (8-6)

indicatorNotes.face: the face of a word is its front letter

blocks.note: saving = except, as bar is: 'all saving one'

annotation.surface: A drunk looks happy about a pub adding an extra hour of drinking time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a pub in the surface, but it means 'except', and so does the old-fashioned SAVING.
annotation.definitionFit: Daylight saving puts the clocks forward an hour in summer.

entries.clue: Contract’s approach we really dislike (4,4,4)

annotation.surface: Everyone hates the way this contract was negotiated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a deal; it is the verb for catching an illness.
annotation.definitionFit: Contract here is the verb for catching an illness, and this phrasal verb says the same about flu or a cold.

entries.clue: Unexpected ciao welcomes sailor docked in French port (7)

indicatorNotes.Unexpected: the letters of CIAO arrive in an unexpected order
indicatorNotes.welcomes: the shuffled word takes JAC in
indicatorNotes.docked: a docked tail is cut short, so JACK loses its end

blocks.note: JACK (a sailor, as in Jack Tar) cut short

annotation.surface: A surprise greeting for a sailor whose ship has tied up at a French harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Docked' fits a sailor in port perfectly, and means cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: Ajaccio is the chief port of Corsica, which is French.

entries.clue: Record translation of Sino-US conference (10)

indicatorNotes.translation of: the letters are translated into a new order

annotation.surface: Minutes are kept of an interpreter's version of a China–America summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Translation' is exactly what a Sino-US summit needs, which hides its job as a letter-shuffler.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a conference is a meeting for talking things over, which is what this word names.

entries.clue: Criminal needing medical assistance in city, avoiding NY somehow (7)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: the letters N and Y are avoided, left out
indicatorNotes.somehow: they are not together, so have to be picked out in some way

blocks.note: IN CITY with N and Y removed
the letters N and Y, taken out of 'in city'

annotation.surface: A sick criminal needs a doctor in town but keeps clear of New York.
annotation.walkthrough: The N and Y leave 'in city' as separate letters, not as New York.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something forbidden by law, as in illicit drugs, is criminal.

entries.clue: Enjoy Moonstruck very much (4,5)

annotation.surface: A film fan loved the Cher film Moonstruck.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital M makes Moonstruck look like the film title; it is just 'crazy'.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something like crazy is doing it very much.

entries.clue: End producer’s plans (5)

blocks.note: what brings about an end or goal: the method, from the phrase 'to an end'
plans = intends, a verb in the third person

annotation.surface: A film producer's scheme for the ending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Producer' is a film word here, but the first half is a cryptic take on 'a means to an end'.
annotation.definitionFit: Means bring about an end; someone who means to go plans to.

entries.clue: Very drunk Irish in A&E showing patience (9)

indicatorNotes.in: IR goes in, placed inside A&E between the A and the E

annotation.surface: A very drunk Irishman waits calmly in the emergency department.
annotation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's accident and emergency department. Patience is the British name for the card game Americans call solitaire.
annotation.definitionFit: Solitaire and patience are the same one-player card game.

entries.clue: Minister’s office undecorated on tea clipper, say (12)

blocks.note: a clipper is a kind of ship

annotation.surface: A minister's quarters aboard a tea clipper are left bare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' just sets undecorated after tea. Tea clippers were the fast sailing ships that raced tea home from China.
annotation.definitionFit: By derivation: a chaplain is a minister attached to a college, regiment or hospital, and the suffix -ship names the post.

entries.clue: Regular publication of poetry beginning to appear in danger (10)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the first letter of appear is used
indicatorNotes.in: ODIC and A go inside PERIL

annotation.surface: A poetry magazine is in danger of folding.
annotation.walkthrough: ODIC, meaning of an ode, is a word mostly met in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a magazine or journal appearing weekly, monthly or quarterly is issued on a regular schedule.

entries.clue: Edward made one sandwiches, still needing improvement? (8)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the outer word holds ED like bread round a filling

annotation.surface: Edward makes someone sandwiches, but his cooking could be better.
annotation.walkthrough: Unedited text has not been improved by an editor yet, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: An unedited draft still needs an editor's improvement.

entries.clue: Suspect English cat pees, jumping on laps? (14)

indicatorNotes.Suspect: the letters are dubious, not to be trusted in their order

annotation.surface: A cat is accused of urinating while leaping onto people's laps.
annotation.walkthrough: Laps suggest a cat on someone's knee; they are circuits of a racecourse.
annotation.definitionFit: Steeplechasing is racing over jumps, lap after lap.

entries.clue: Set off and wandered widely, now distant (9)

indicatorNotes.off: SET goes off, out of its order

annotation.surface: Someone who left and roamed the world has drifted away from home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as setting out on a journey; split, it is SET made to go off.
annotation.definitionFit: Estranged means no longer close, distant.

entries.clue: Sailor’s house given navy telephone (10)

blocks.note: surface padding: the house is given the navy, just joining the pieces
the blower is British slang for the telephone

annotation.surface: A sailor's house has a navy-issue phone.
annotation.walkthrough: Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's fictional naval officer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Horatio, hero of C. S. Forester's naval novels, rises from midshipman to admiral.

entries.clue: The way scarf occupies empty seat in grandstand (8)

indicatorNotes.occupies: HOW and BOA sit inside ST
indicatorNotes.empty: SEAT emptied of its middle leaves S and T

blocks.note: a boa is a feather scarf

annotation.surface: A spectator leaves a scarf on an empty seat in the stand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grandstand' is at the end and looks like the stadium; it is the verb meaning to play to the crowd.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both verbs mean showing off to spectators to win applause.

entries.clue: Tiny chap one can only imagine developing herculean power (10)

annotation.definition: Tiny chap one can only imagine

indicatorNotes.developing: the letters develop into a new form

annotation.surface: A small man can only dream of becoming mighty.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the long first half: a leprechaun exists only in the imagination.
annotation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is a tiny imaginary man of Irish folklore.

entries.clue: Wearing big top for one purpose (6)

blocks.note: in = wearing, as in 'in a hat'
a big top is a circus tent

annotation.surface: Dressing for the circus has a purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' says the big top is one example of a TENT.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: intent names an aim or goal, as in 'with intent to kill'.

entries.clue: 24 hours too long without company (10)

annotation.surface: Spending a whole day alone feels endless.
annotation.walkthrough: '24 hours' looks like a cross-reference to 24 across, but it is just a day, here Friday.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: having no friends leaves someone alone, lacking companions.

entries.clue: German before unification coming back through Ossi’s sewer (5)

indicatorNotes.through: the answer runs through the words

blocks.note: hidden in osSI'S SEWer, read backwards

annotation.surface: A West German comes home through an East German's drain.
annotation.walkthrough: Ossi and Wessi were German slang for East and West Germans; the clue sets the pair side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A Wessi was a West German, a citizen before reunification.

entries.clue: Different twins who start to examine who’s the fairest? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Different: the letters end up different in order
indicatorNotes.start to: only the first letter of examine is used

annotation.surface: Two unlike twins want someone to judge which one is prettier.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the queen's mirror: 'Who is the fairest of them all?' The answer is Snow White.
annotation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the mirror names Snow White as the fairest of all.

entries.clue: Fall out of bed, turning over fourteen pounds towards scam (4,1,4,3,2)

indicatorNotes.turning over: FALL and UP are turned round

blocks.note: a stone is 14 lb, so 'fourteen pounds' is A STONE

annotation.surface: A sleeper falls out of bed and piles on the weight.
annotation.walkthrough: FALL UP reversed gives PULLAF. A stone, 14 pounds, is the British unit for body weight.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to trick someone by deceit, which is what a scam does to its victim.

entries.clue: 950 year-old in several books, not one that explains it (4)

blocks.note: no = not one, as in 'no reason'
'Ah!' is what one says when something is explained

annotation.surface: An ancient figure appears in many books, none of which explain his great age.
annotation.walkthrough: Genesis gives Noah 950 years, and he is mentioned in several books of the Bible.
annotation.definitionFit: Noah lived 950 years, according to Genesis.

entries.clue: Big craft project involves me carrying work around (5,3)

indicatorNotes.involves: to involve is to enfold or include, so JUT includes the rest inside it
indicatorNotes.carrying: to carry is to hold, so ME holds the reversed word between its letters
indicatorNotes.around: turned around means facing the other way, so JOB is read backwards

annotation.surface: A large craft project involves the speaker taking on extra work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft project' sounds like knitting; 'craft' is an aircraft and 'project' a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A jumbo jet is a very large aircraft.

entries.clue: Party stuff put up with energy (8)

annotation.surface: Party supplies were raised with gusto.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as hoisting decorations; it means endured, BORE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: originally a large gathering of Scouts, now any lively celebration or festivity.

entries.clue: Split pin opening for steelworker? (5,4)

blocks.note: a thole is a pin holding an oar

annotation.surface: A split pin is a steelworker's handy item.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Split pin' looks like one object; the break falls a letter later than it seems. A thole pin holds an oar in place.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: steel girders were joined by hammering rivets through holes drilled for them.

entries.clue: Parking suitable for homes of top US executive (12)

blocks.note: P = parking, as on road signs

annotation.surface: Parking for residents' houses in the grounds of a top US executive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top US executive' is the President, the head of the executive branch.
annotation.definitionFit: By derivation: the adjective formed from president, the head of America's executive branch.

entries.clue: A little smoke from oil and garlic cooking (9)

indicatorNotes.cooking: the letters are cooked, mixed together

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 'and' just joins the two

annotation.surface: A bit of smoke rises when oil and garlic are cooking.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen smoke is a little cigar.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a small thin cigar, the diminutive ending -illo marking its size.

entries.clue: Rope around branch could make tree this (9)

indicatorNotes.around: a rope goes around a branch, and so CABLE wraps around LIMB

blocks.note: a cable is a thick rope
a limb is a large branch

annotation.surface: Tying a rope round a branch makes a tree easy to scale.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's end: a rope round a branch could make the tree climbable, so the whole clue reads as a true statement.
annotation.definitionFit: A rope round a branch makes a tree climbable.

entries.clue: One’s tablet possibly reduced channels for movies (8)

indicatorNotes.reduced: MEDIA is cut short by its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone's tablet computer has fewer channels for watching films.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' and 'channels' suggest a streaming device; the tablet is a pill.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pill or tablet is one form in which drugs are taken.

entries.clue: Exchange prisoners sent over (4)

indicatorNotes.sent over: something sent over is flipped end over end, so the word reads backwards

annotation.surface: A prisoner exchange across the border.
annotation.walkthrough: SWOP is the British spelling variant of swap.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: this spelling variant of swap names a trade of one thing for another.

entries.clue: Learner interrupts agricultural class making joke (10)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: L breaks into the other word

blocks.note: the peasantry are the farming class

annotation.surface: A student cracks a joke that interrupts a farming lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a school lesson but is a social class.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pleasantry is a light remark or jest made in polite conversation.

entries.clue: Vile knitwear one drops in chute (4,6)

annotation.surface: An ugly sweater is dropped into a laundry chute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chute' is a parachute, and a jumper is a sweater in British English.
annotation.definitionFit: A base jumper leaps off buildings and drops under a parachute.

entries.clue: River king leaves during twilight (5)

annotation.surface: A king leaves the river bank as the light fades.
annotation.walkthrough: IN DUSK loses its K.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this great waterway flows from Tibet through Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.

entries.clue: Rum toffee Charlie put down as secret weakness (4,2,4)

indicatorNotes.Rum: rum = odd, so the letters come out oddly

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Charlie hides his secret weakness for rum toffee.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum toffee looks like a sweet; 'rum' means strange and shuffles TOFFEE.
annotation.definitionFit: Feet of clay are a hidden flaw in someone admired.

entries.clue: Better being taken care of with humility (3,2,4)

annotation.surface: Things improve when handled humbly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, CAP.
annotation.definitionFit: Going cap in hand means asking humbly.

entries.clue: Nearly all plugs function as solution for drips, perhaps (6)

indicatorNotes.plugs: a plug fills a hole, so AL fills a gap inside SINE

annotation.surface: Plumbing: fixing nearly every drip.
annotation.walkthrough: Drips here are hospital IV drips, not leaks.
annotation.definitionFit: Saline is the salt solution used in hospital drips.

entries.clue: Malicious flying bomb to be destroyed (8)

blocks.note: the V-1 flying bomb of WWII

annotation.surface: A malicious flying bomb is set to be destroyed.
annotation.walkthrough: The V-1 or doodlebug is written VI here, as in the Roman-numeral look.
annotation.definitionFit: By derivation: like a viper, a venomous snake, so spiteful and full of venom.

entries.clue: British countryside somewhat flatter (8)

annotation.surface: British countryside is rather flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like 'more flat', a description of landscape; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to coax someone with flattery and cajoling words.

entries.clue: Shellfish baby shelled unaided (7)

annotation.surface: A baby shelling seafood by itself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' fits shellfish, which hides its job of stripping BABY to AB.
annotation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail, a shellfish.

entries.clue: Rambling on, press one’s point, showing sensitivity (14)

indicatorNotes.Rambling: the letters ramble out of order

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, a point

annotation.surface: Someone rambles on, pressing a point, trying to show they care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' stands for 'one has', which becomes I'VE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: quickness to react to others' feelings, being receptive and alert.

entries.clue: Critique to do with struggle for superiority — women’s (6)

annotation.surface: A critic writes about a feminist struggle for supremacy.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash leaves 'women's' dangling like a possessive; it is just W.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a written assessment of a book, film or performance.

entries.clue: Mind boudoir having limited shower pressure? (10)

indicatorNotes.having: BOWER holds the rest inside it
indicatorNotes.limited: pressure is cut down to its first letter

blocks.note: a bower is a lady's private room

annotation.surface: Someone worries about poor water pressure in the bedroom shower.
annotation.walkthrough: The bathroom picture hides a weather shower, RAIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: intellectual capacity, the thinking ability of the brain.

entries.clue: Leak in tin cask concerning — one sounds the alarm shortly (6,6)

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a butt is a large cask

annotation.surface: A dripping barrel worries someone, who will soon raise the alarm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leak in tin' is read loosely, the leak joined onto tin's symbol. The snooze button makes the alarm clock sound again shortly.
annotation.definitionFit: A snooze button sets the alarm to ring again after a short delay.

entries.clue: Lots of deliveries during term for boarders? (5)

indicatorNotes.term for: a term is an end, so the last letter of boarders

annotation.surface: Parcels pile up at a boarding school in term time.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, or deliveries; the surface makes them parcels at school.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword-flavoured sense: in cricket each set of six balls bowled is one over, so many of them mean many deliveries.

entries.clue: Mark in Spanish up to 40% of grade (5)

indicatorNotes.40% of: two of GRADE's five letters, taken from the end

blocks.note: the last two of GRADE's five letters

annotation.surface: A Spanish exam mark worth up to 40% of the final grade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as an exam score; it is the accent over the Spanish ñ.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the wavy accent written over the n of Spanish words such as senor.

entries.clue: Judge elected, by bad luck (4)

annotation.surface: A judge owes his post to plain bad luck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' is the multiplication sign: a room measured three by four is 3 x 4.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a jinx is a curse or run of misfortune blamed on someone or something.

entries.clue: Environmentally friendly lithium cells we have inside, naturally (1,4)

blocks.note: Li is the symbol for lithium

annotation.surface: Green lithium batteries built into things, naturally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lithium cells' looks like batteries; the cells are bacteria living in the gut.
annotation.definitionFit: E. coli bacteria live naturally in the human gut.

entries.clue: Knock out every other pair in semi-finals — top class fencing that (9)

indicatorNotes.every other pair in: SE MI FI NA LS: take the second and fourth pairs
indicatorNotes.fencing: a fence encloses a field, so ELITE encloses the letter pairs

blocks.note: the elite are the top class
seMIfiNAls, every other pair of letters

annotation.surface: In a tournament, the top seeds knock out others in the semi-finals.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters are read in pairs, not singly: se-MI-fi-NA-ls.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in a tournament both mean remove a competitor from further rounds.

entries.clue: Someone who gets their post through you? (7)

annotation.definition: Someone who gets their post through you?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a person whose mail arrives
the setter's reading: a post, or stake, driven through your body

annotation.surface: A postman delivering letters to you.
annotation.walkthrough: The post sounds like mail through a letterbox; it is a stake driven through a body, as Vlad the Impaler did.
annotation.definitionFit: An impaler drives a stake, or post, through a victim.

entries.clue: Fastener that’s melted on Spooner’s cycling bags (7,3)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: wheeling = cycling; its W sound is traded for the S of the next word
sacks = bags; its S sound is traded for the W, giving WACKS

annotation.surface: A bike pannier's clasp has melted.
annotation.walkthrough: Wheeling is cycling and sacks are bags; swap their first sounds.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this red resin was heated and dripped onto envelopes, then stamped to seal them shut.

entries.clue: Din curtailed school debate, on giving away uniform free (9)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: curtailed literally means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.giving away: giving something away means parting with it, so the word loses that letter

blocks.note: U = uniform in the phonetic alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Noise cut short a school debate about letting pupils ditch uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' puts ARGE after the other pieces. 'Uniform' reads as school clothes; it is U.
annotation.definitionFit: To discharge someone is to release them, set them free.
